title: A2UI Protocol Message (v1.0)
description: Expresses the A2UI v1.0 agent-to-renderer protocol defined by a2ui-project/a2ui (Apache-2.0). This repo does NOT define A2UI; this file encodes someone else's protocol so constraint validation has a deterministic local source of truth. Upstream authority: https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui — specification/v1_0/docs/a2ui_protocol.md (envelope model), specification/v1_0/common_types.json (ComponentCommon, DynamicString), specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json (component vocabulary). Re-verify via Context7 library id /a2ui-project/a2ui before editing. Structural rules JSON Schema cannot express — acyclicity of the component id-reference graph, reachability from the root, and catalog membership — are enforced by scripts/normalize-a2ui.mjs, not here.

version.description: Protocol version. v1.0 is the version this schema encodes.

surfaceId.description: Identifies the surface an operation applies to.

componentId.description: Unique within a surface. Referenced by `child` / `children` from other components.

componentName.description: PascalCase component name. Upstream constrains this to the declared catalog; the pattern here is a shape check only. Catalog membership is enforced by scripts/normalize-a2ui.mjs, which cannot be expressed in JSON Schema without inlining a catalog.

dynamicString.description: A leaf value: either a literal JSON primitive, or a {"path": "/pointer"} reference resolved against the surface dataModel. Anything else — notably an expression object — is rejected.

child.description: Single child, by id. Never an inline object — the component list is flat.

children.description: Ordered child ids. Never inline objects.

anyOf.description: Guard: `type` was the pre-alignment dialect's discriminator. Upstream uses `component`.
Guard: `bindings` was the pre-alignment dialect's data model. Upstream uses dataModel + {"path": …}.

component.description: One component. Structural keys (id, component, child, children) are fixed; every other property is catalog-specific and must be a dynamicString leaf, a plain object/array of them, or a literal. This is what closes the expression-binding hole: an unconstrained property would let {'kind':'expression'} through, which is the arbitrary-JS hazard assess Q3 flagged.

componentArray.description: FLAT array. Parent-child structure is expressed by id reference, not nesting.

catalogId.description: Identifies the component catalog this surface is authored against.

updateComponents.description: Merges by component id into an existing surface. Does not replace the surface.

callFunction.description: Accepted structurally so a conformant stream validates. Round-tripping is out of scope for this repo's v1 (see p8-04).

dynamicStringOrStructure.description: A catalog-specific property value. anyOf, not oneOf: a {"path": …} leaf legitimately matches both the dynamicString branch and the generic-object branch, and oneOf would reject it for matching twice. The expression guard is applied to every object branch instead, so the arbitrary-JS hazard (assess Q3) is closed regardless of which branch matches.
